significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, under referential ambiguity, truth value and item binding are separable causal contributors to belief behavior: probe-detected mis-binding predicts errors, the "binding-error rate" grows with item similarity and context length, and re-routing binding repairs answers "without changing the truth-value representation." This combines a form-(iii) predictive/scaling relation with a form-(ii) causal decomposition, fixing expectations for harder multi-item contexts and distinguishing failures of entity attribution from failures of truth encoding; Feng and Steinhardt's 2023 entity-binding work shows that binding variables are already a consequential mechanistic framework for contextual representations. It establishes both a phenomenon and mechanism, while a verified-false result would informatively rule out separable item-truth binding as an explanation of these belief errors; the branches are determinate despite the hedge that binding may explain only "many" failures. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit: merely asking how LLMs represent item-specific beliefs would not supply this binding/truth double dissociation, predictive coupling, or scaling claim.

reach.justification: The claim hands over three named handles: an "item-conditioned belief probe," a "binding-error rate metric," and a "lightweight attention-based re-binding intervention" that is asserted to reduce belief errors while preserving factual QA. The probe can be ex ante when read before answer generation—its mis-binding is claimed to be "predictive of behavioral belief errors"—and the re-binding intervention gives auditors or inference-system builders an action window rather than merely explaining an error afterward. After model-specific re-extraction, the conclusion predicts more than the existence of another direction: binding-error rate should increase with item similarity and context length, although the intervention target itself would still require rediscovery and the stated scope is limited to multi-item referential-ambiguity belief tasks rather than all belief behavior. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score, because the general topic supplies neither a forecastable binding metric nor a corrective routing handle; these claim-specific outputs could be used by researchers and practitioners auditing or gating ambiguous-context responses.
